era_setting.place: Kansas City, Missouri, USA (and St. Louis, Missouri, for the 1988 Court of Appeals)
era_setting.notes: The film runs from the design and fabrication of the walkways in 1978-79 to the Missouri Court of Appeals decision of 26 January 1988. OUT OF PERIOD, and therefore wrong in any cut: mobile phones, flat-panel monitors, LED site lighting, modern hi-vis PPE, cordless power tools, post-1990 vehicles, laptop computers, CAD screens, and any building with a glass curtain wall of a kind that does not exist in a 1980 American city. OUT OF PLACE: a European plaza, an Asian street, EU or UK number plates, foreign-language signage, left-hand-drive/right-hand-drive mismatch, and above all any recognisable modern hotel atrium marketed as itself. Declared because EP62 greene shipped a 2011 Range Rover on an EU plate and EP63 shipped modern clips through five green gates, purely because nothing machine-readable said what century or continent the film was in. NOTE for the human screen: this episode's archive registers are steel, drafting, construction and civic architecture, all of which are dominated on the shelf by 2015-2024 footage. Period-plausibility is the single most likely failure here and no machine gate measures it.

forbidden_claims: as built the connection had only 31 percent of the strength the code required -- nbs's 31 percent is a LOAD ratio (21.4 kips actually on the connection against the 68 kips of ultimate capacity the code expected). the as-built CAPACITY ratio is 18.6 against 68, about 27 percent, nbs never states it, and it must be labelled as our arithmetic. the missouri court of appeals makes exactly this slip in its own footnote 12 and that footnote must not be quoted for the engineering

the two-rod change was the cause of the collapse, said flatly and alone -- nbs names two contributing factors and puts the inadequacy of the original design first; the original single-rod detail also failed the kansas city building code at about 60 percent of required capacity
any explanation of why nbs counts 113 dead in may 1982 and the missouri court of appeals counts 114 in 1988 -- no retrieved document explains it. use 114, cite the court, do not narrate the gap
216 injured, or any injury figure other than nbs's 188 (of whom two died), the court's at least 186, or ascé's nearly 200

dramatising the telephone call between havens and the engineers -- it is in neither the federal report nor the appellate opinion. what the record establishes is that the change was transmitted to duncan and approved, and that he assured an architect it was sound

attributing 142,000 pounds or about seventy-one tons to nbs -- 142,000 lb is the missouri court of appeals' figure, and the seventy-one-ton reconstruction from nbs's measured 17.8 kips per span is ours
the victims received $78 million, or any figure presented as the final civil recovery -- over $78,000,000 is what insurers had paid out as at december 1983 and litigation continued afterwards

the walkways were crowded with dancers and the dancing shook them down -- nbs conclusion 1(c) excludes dynamic loads from walking or dancing, and nbs's credible upper bound for both collapsed walkways combined is 63 people

calling the box beam-hanger rod connection a bolt, a weld or a bracket -- it is a 1 1/4-inch threaded rod through a hole in a box beam made of two 8-inch channels, bearing on a nut and a washer, and the failure mode is the rod and washer pulling through the beam

any third-party broadcast, news or press footage or photograph of the event, including the kmbc tv videotape and the kansas city star and kansas city times photographs, in any form, blurred, cropped, behind a graphic or as a single frame
any generated or recreated image depicting a body, an injured person, blood, a covered casualty, a rescue in progress, or debris with a person under it
any depiction of the crowded lobby at, or in the seconds before, the moment of collapse, from any angle, including from above, including in silhouette, including abstracted
naming any victim or survivor, or depicting the likeness of any real person -- victim, survivor, rescuer, witness, judge, board member or engineer

making any generated image look like an authentic record: a photograph of drawing s405.1 or shop drawing 30, a page of the 442-page commission decision, a missouri professional engineer's seal carrying a real name or the real state seal artwork, an nbs test photograph, a newspaper front page, a court exhibit, or a videotape frame with a timecode

any claim about daniel duncan's or jack gillum's state of mind, motive, character, finances or private life beyond the findings of the administrative hearing commission and the missouri court of appeals -- specifically he knew it would fall, he did not care, he was cutting costs, he was chasing fees, he lied to save money, and any interior monologue or imagined scene

blaming the architect, the contractor, havens steel company, the city of kansas city or the hotel owner -- no tribunal in the retrieved record made a finding against any of them, and the missouri board did not investigate the architects at all

quoting the duncan opinion's summary of a party's argument as if it were the court's own finding, and above all reading gillum's cross-examination answer as narration rather than as attributed testimony

the engineers went to prison, were convicted, or were criminally charged -- in december 1983 the county prosecutor and the u.s. attorney announced that no criminal charges would be filed. a state licensing board revoked their licences and they were the first american engineers to lose a licence for gross negligence
the asce expelled him -- the ethics committee recommended expulsion, the board of direction voted a three-year suspension, and he then relinquished membership himself
any statement about what duncan or gillum is doing now, where they live, whether they are alive, or what they think today -- the freshest retrieved information is from 1994-95
describing nbs building science series 143 as the nist report, or dating it to anything but may 1982 -- the national bureau of standards did not become nist until 1988

any statement that the kansas city building code, missouri licensing law, aisc practice or asce practice changed BECAUSE of this collapse -- nothing retrieved establishes a causal change, and the 1976 asce canon predates the event

notes: RUNTIME AND WORD BANDS ARE DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN. Pace basis is docs/PD_CANON.md rule 25: the measured end-to-end band is 159.5-169.7 wpm, and EP66's delivered master is 4,278 words / 1604.211 s = 160.0 wpm. The narration tool's own 'measured wpm' (171.8 on EP66) counts speech only and excludes inter-chunk silence; it is 7% fast and is NOT used here. WORD BAND: writing band 4,400-5,000, design centre 4,700; the delivered script measures 4,692 narration words (check_script_craft, 2026-08-11). RUNTIME BAND, derived at both edges so it holds across the whole measured pace range: R_lo = 60*4400/169.7 + 9.0 = 1555.7 + 9.0 = 1564.7 s (fewest words at the fastest measured pace); R_hi = 60*5000/159.5 + 9.0 = 1880.9 + 9.0 = 1889.9 s (most words at the slowest). Declared band [1560, 1895] contains both edges. DESIGN POINT: 4,692 words spans 1658.8 s (169.7 wpm) to 1765.0 s (159.5 wpm); this film also carries 30.0 s of DESIGNED SILENCE that is not narration -- 22.0 s for the H2 connection assembly, 2.5 s at the TURN, 2.5 s of black after 7:05 PM, and 3.0 s of H5 -- plus ENDCARD_SEC 9.0 with leadSeconds 0. Finished film therefore lands 1697.8-1804.0 s (28:18-30:04), inside the declared band at both edges. CUT BUDGET, checked so the contract is satisfiable (EP66 declared one that was not): at target_cut_sec 3.6 the film holds 1560/3.6 = 433 cuts at the short edge and 1895/3.6 = 526 at the long edge; stills may occupy at most 32% of cuts, so still cuts are <= 138 at the short edge and video cuts are >= 295 there. mandatory_stills 113 fits under 138 and distinct_video_assets 250 fits under 295, at BOTH edges. PLATE COUNT IS DERIVED FROM THE SCRIPT'S OWN SECTION WORD COUNTS, one commissioned plate per 45 narration words per section, rounded up, with a floor of 6 for the HOOK and 2 for the OP because those two sections cut far faster than the film's average: HOOK 56w->6, OP 33w->2, ACT_1 722w->17, ACT_2 882w->20, ACT_3 779w->18, ACT_4 980w->22, ACT_5 1069w->24, ENDING 171w->4. Total 113.
